## Open Source Philosophy

I am a strong believer in the power of open source software to democratize technology and accelerate innovation. My open source work has been primarily focused on developer tools, machine learning infrastructure, and streamlining production workflows. I've been fortunate to contribute to widely-used projects such as [fastai](#fastai), [Metaflow](#metaflow), [Kubeflow](#kubeflow), [Jupyter](#jupyter), and [Great Expectations](#great-expectations).

Below is a detailed overview of my contributions and the projects I maintain.

## ![fastai logo](img_oss/fastai_small.png){width="10%"} fastai

The fastai library is one of the most popular high-level frameworks for deep learning. I maintain and contribute to a variety of [fastai](https://github.com/fastai) projects, focusing on improving the developer experience and expanding the library's capabilities. Below are the specific projects I've been deeply involved in:

::: {#fastai-listings}
:::


## ![Metaflow logo](img_oss/metaflow.webp){width="7%"} Metaflow

Metaflow is a framework for real-life data science. I created [notebook cards](https://github.com/outerbounds/metaflow-card-notebook): A tool that allows you to use notebooks to generate reports, visualizations, and diagnostics directly within Metaflow production workflows. This helps bridge the gap between experimental notebooks and production-grade monitoring. You can read more about it on the [official blog](https://outerbounds.com/blog/notebooks-in-production-with-metaflow/).

## ![Kubeflow logo](img_oss/kubeflow.jpeg){width="10%"} Kubeflow

Kubeflow is the machine learning toolkit for Kubernetes. I've worked on several projects related to Kubeflow, mainly focusing on building practical examples and enhancing documentation to help developers deploy ML models more effectively:

::: {#kubeflow-listings}
:::


## ![Jupyter logo](img_oss/jupyter.png){width="7%"} Jupyter

I created the [Repo2Docker GitHub Action](https://github.com/jupyterhub/repo2docker-action), which allows you to trigger [repo2docker](https://github.com/jupyter/repo2docker) to build Jupyter-enabled Docker images directly from your GitHub repository. This Action is essential for teams looking to pre-cache images for their own [BinderHub cluster](https://binderhub.readthedocs.io/en/latest/zero-to-binderhub/setup-binderhub.html) or for sharing reproducible environments on [mybinder.org](https://mybinder.org/).

This project was recognized for its utility and accepted into the official JupyterHub GitHub organization.

## ![Great Expectations logo](img_oss/ge-logo.png){width="7%"} Great Expectations

Data quality is paramount in machine learning. I developed the [Great Expectations GitHub Action](https://github.com/great-expectations/great_expectations_action) to enable automated data validation within CI/CD workflows. This ensures that data pipelines remain healthy and that schema changes or data drift are caught early. More details can be found in this [GitHub Blog post](https://github.blog/2020-10-01-keeping-your-data-pipelines-healthy-with-the-great-expectations-github-action/).
